english.title: Fail to comply with a section 49 notice to disclose the key to protected information
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being required to disclose a key, namely **(..SPECIFY THE KEY OR KEYWORD..), to protected information, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INFORMATION..), by a notice issued under Section 49 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000, knowingly failed, in accordance with the notice, to make the disclosure required
english.legislation: Contrary to section 53(1) and (5) of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.

english.notes:
(i) See section 53(4) for defence
(ii) See section 56(1) for an interpretation of "key","protected information" and "Section 49 notice".
(iii) Section 15 of the Terrorism Act 2006 increased the maximum penalty in a national security case to five years for offences committed AFTER 13th April 2006.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

Indictment: In a case of national security: Five years imprisonment and / or a fine. "In any other case: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Offences committed before 13th April 2006: Two years imprisonment and / or fine in all cases.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
